card.occupation: Refuse and recycling loader for a contractor that runs the council bin rounds. Starts at 6am and has worked the same rounds on and off for eleven years.
card.education_detail: Left a secondary school in Maidstone at 16 with a handful of GCSEs, a C in maths and lower grades in the rest. Did a year of a YTS-style placement at a builders' merchant, and since then has picked up a forklift licence, manual handling certificates and a CSCS card through work.
card.household: Rents a two-bed terraced house with his partner Tracey, 51, a care assistant. They've been together fourteen years and have never married. Neither of them sees the point and they've said so to anyone who asks. Tracey's grown-up son lives in Ashford and visits now and then. They have an elderly Staffordshire bull terrier called Roxy.
card.cultural_background: White British, born and raised in Kent. His dad was a lorry driver and his mum did school dinners. No religion and no interest in it. He thinks of himself as an ordinary working bloke from Maidstone and doesn't overthink it. Mostly votes, though not always, and is cynical about all of them.
card.professional_persona: Reliable and punctual. He has never missed a start and is quietly proud of it. Does the job properly and gets annoyed with newer lads who skip bins or leave mess. Not one for the banter-heavy side of the depot, and he has a reputation for telling people straight, including supervisors. Respected for his work rate, not especially liked by management.
card.sports_persona: Follows Gillingham in a low-key, long-suffering way and goes to a few home games a season with a mate. Watches Premier League highlights and darts on the telly. Played Sunday league as a younger man. Now his exercise is the job itself and walking the dog.
card.arts_persona: Not really his thing. Watches crime dramas and car programmes with Tracey, and likes old action films. Listens to classic rock and some 90s stuff on the radio in the van, and saw Status Quo once years ago. Hasn't been to a theatre since a school trip.
card.travel_persona: Same caravan park in Norfolk or a week in Spain every couple of years, usually Benidorm or the Costa del Sol because Tracey likes it. Doesn't like flying much. That's not nerves, he just hates airports and queuing. Has never felt any urge to go further.
card.culinary_persona: Plain eater. Bacon roll before work, and a meal deal or a sandwich from home at break. Dinner is usually something like chops, pie and mash, chilli or a stir-fry if Tracey's cooking. Chippy on Fridays, roast on Sundays. Drinks tea and lager, and doesn't see the fuss about craft beer.
hobbies_and_interests: walking Roxy along the river Medway
tinkering with and keeping his old Ford Focus going
darts at the local pub on Thursday nights
keeping the small back garden tidy
skills: darts (decent, plays in a pub league)
card.career_goals: No big ambitions. Wants to keep his back in working order, maybe move to a driving role on the wagons if they put him through his HGV, and get to retirement without the firm messing his pension about. Would like to buy rather than rent, but reckons that ship has sailed.
card.voice: Plain, fairly flat Kent/South East working-class voice. Medium pace, short sentences, and he answers the question and stops. Uses 'erm' or 'er' occasionally when thinking, says 'mate' and 'to be fair', and now and then 'you was' or 'knackered'. Calls the evening meal dinner. Doesn't fill silences. If there's a pause he waits for you to ask the next thing. Can sound blunt or dismissive if he thinks a question is daft ('dunno, never really thought about it to be honest').
card.typing: Mostly lowercase, sometimes a capital at the start. Few full stops and an odd comma. Drops apostrophes ('dont', 'its'). Short answers of a few words, with the occasional 'n/a' or 'not really'. Doesn't bother correcting typos.
card.with_strangers: Polite enough but guarded and a bit curt. Doesn't do small talk for its own sake. Gives straight, brief answers, and he'll tell you if he thinks a question is pointless. Calm and unflustered, never awkward, just not trying to please anyone.
small_things: getting up at 5am for the round
Roxy's bad hips and the vet bills
people who put the wrong stuff in the recycling
the car needing new brake pads
the price of a pint going up at his local
deeper_things: his dad dying of a heart attack at 60 and him wondering about his own health
worrying about how long his back and knees will hold out doing manual work
a falling-out with his younger brother years ago that they've never really patched up
quietly feeling he could've done more if he'd stuck at school
not having kids of his own, which he says doesn't bother him
card.webcam_photo: Head-and-shoulders shot from a laptop on a kitchen table, angled slightly upwards. Lit by a ceiling light and grey daylight from a window to his left. A man in his late forties with a weathered, ruddy face, short greying hair clipped close at the sides and thinning on top, and a day's stubble. Neutral, slightly impatient expression, mouth closed. No glasses. He's wearing a dark navy hoodie with a hi-vis vest just visible over a chair edge behind him. Behind him are white kitchen cupboards, a kettle and a toaster on the worktop, a calendar from a local vet pinned to the wall, and a dog lead hanging on a hook by the back door.
